newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai rubber prices up on active short-covering.
newsitem.headline: Thai rubber prices up on active short-covering.

text.p: Thai rubber prices edged up slightly this week on active buying and news that the Japan's end-January rubber stock dropped on month, industry sources said on Wednesday.
The firmer prices have triggered short-covering, mostly among Japanese buyers, they said.
Chinese buyers also entered the market this week to cover their positions ahead of Chinese New Year holiday.
"Buying activities picked up from last week. Perhaps weak offer prices last week attracted buyers," said a Hat Yai-based trader. "News of lower stock in Japan also boosted sentiment," he added.
Japan's end-January rubber stock was recorded at 41,599 tonnes compared with 43,244 tonnes in December.
Benchmark RSS3 for March shipment was quoted around $1.19 kg FOB Bangkok on Wednesday from around $1.18 on the same basis last week.
Latex was quoted around $0.92 a kg for March deliveries.
